thread:
mina: Quick follow-up to the RFC thread: ops needs a concrete 'signal fusion' design for canary + A/B auto-fallbacks. Key constraints: minimize false positives, make investigations easy, and avoid cache/affinity regressions when flipping.

joel: Agreed. My proposal is a two-layer detector: a fast EWMA-based alerting layer for realtime spikes, plus a slower Bayesian stability scorer that accumulates evidence before action.

ram: Love the idea. Can we make the fast layer only generate warnings that feed the scorer? Only the scorer can trigger an automatic fallback. That avoids single blips causing swaps.

anya: Also add provenance weights. Signals from synthetic golden prompts should bump the prior more than a noisy user metric. Suggest weight mapping: golden=5, synthetic=3, user=1.

ops-bot: [notice] canary v10 deployed to 3 regions; perf monitor started. :robot_face:

mina: On regional skew: compute per-region stability_score, then apply a quorum rule: require 50%+ of healthy regions to show degradation OR a global score > threshold. This prevents one noisy POP from tripping a global fallback.

joel: For affinity/KV warmup, we should perform a short shadow-warmup phase before committing full traffic. Steps: mirror 1% for 2m with prefix-affinity, then 5% for 3m. If warmup metrics look OK, allow full flip. Mirror should incrementally pre-populate KV entries.

ram: Here's a compact scoring sketch:
```
# for each minute:
metric_z = (value - baseline)/stddev
ewma = alpha*metric_z + (1-alpha)*prev_ewma
bayes_evidence += weight * logistic(ewma - trigger_t)
if bayes_evidence > bayes_threshold:
  trigger_fallback(idempotency_token)
```
Use alpha=0.3 default, bayes_threshold tuned by experiments.

anya: Important: record sample sizes and confidence intervals. If p95 is noisy with n<1000, downweight it. The scorer should expose a confidence field so UI can say "high/medium/low confidence" when auto-fallback happens.

casey: Router contract: support POST /runtime/fallbacks with body {variant_from, variant_to, reason, token} and GET /runtime/fallbacks/{id}/status. The API must be idempotent and return the chosen mirror ramp plan if accepted.

mina: Also include a lightweight "safety hold" TTL: automatic fallbacks enter a 10m hold where further auto-fallbacks are suppressed unless operator clears or evidence grows 3x. Manual fallback resets the hold.

joel: Circuit breather: each auto-fallback doubles the minimum cool_down (10m -> 20m -> 40m) up to a cap. That prevents oscillation across close calls. Manual overrides zero the multiplier.

ram: Observability: store trigger payloads with: metrics snapshot, region map, sample sizes, anchor hash, and decision trace (ewma values, bayes evidence). Keep these for 90d for postmortems.

anya: UX: show "why" panel with top 3 contributing signals and confidence. Allow one-click rehearse: re-run the scorer over historical window with a chosen baseline to test sensitivity.

ops-bot: [action] scheduled a canary-anchor-run (200 deterministic prompts) in 30s.

casey: One security ops ask: per-tenant opt-out flag required for enterprise contracts. Must be checked before auto action for affected tenant-scoped rollouts. Default = allow.

mina: Action items: 1) joel + ram: bench EWMA + bayes parameters and produce a sensitivity matrix, 2) casey + ops: draft router API and idempotency semantics, 3) anya: define anchor weighting and sample size rules, 4) I'll assemble a small runbook for operators (how to inspect, approve, or revert). Deadline: draft RFC next Tue.

joel: I'll add unit tests that inject synthetic noise and regional blips.

ram: We'll simulate cache-warmup benefits with a 0.5% -> 2% ramp and measure cold-hit delta.

anya: I'll propose default thresholds (bayes_threshold=8, trigger_t=1.5) but will include calibration notes.

mina: Thanks team. If no objections I9ll fold this into the RFC. :white_check_mark:
